answer: One defense is stake-weighted reputation tied to verifiable work history. Each agent must lock a deposit and build a thread of auditable tasks before transacting at full limits. A newcomer may whisper offers, but counterparties check its thread: thin history means low trust and small caps. Creating many fake identities requires splitting deposits, paying fees, and doing real work for each one, while a relic of past fraud, such as a revoked credential, follows linked keys and raises future costs. Sybils become expensive, slow, and easy to throttle.
